key_idea: Write e,w = a ± p/2 and n,s = b ± r/2 with a+b = y/2; the objective becomes max(|a|+|p|/2, |b|+|r|/2), a one-dimensional convex problem solved by balancing the two terms and clamping.
sketch: By symmetry take y >= 0 (flip signs of a and b otherwise) and h = y/2. The optimum has a,b in [0,h]: set a = (h+|r|/2-|p|/2)/2 clamped to [0,h] and b = h-a; if the clamp bites, the larger of |p|/2, |r|/2 is already an unavoidable lower bound. Output n=b+r/2, e=a+p/2, s=b-r/2, w=a-p/2. O(1) per query. Any optimal assignment is accepted; sample 1 happens to match token-wise, and I also validated 300 random queries with a script checking the three equations and comparing the max flap against a ternary search of the 1-D objective.
